Enable the Key Vault firewall, set the default action to deny, and allow the specified VNet subnets and the on-premises IP
Configure the Key Vault to allow access from 'All networks' and add a Conditional Access policy restricting Key Vault access
Apply a Network Security Group to the Key Vault's subnet blocking inbound traffic except from the specified subnets and IP
questions.explanation: The Key Vault firewall settings allow you to specify allowed virtual network subnets (using Service Endpoints to extend VNet identity to Key Vault) and specific public IP ranges, with a default action of Deny for all other traffic. The 'Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass' option is important to maintain functionality for Azure services like Azure Backup and ARM deployments. Allowing all networks defeats the purpose. A Private Endpoint disables the public endpoint entirely and does not accommodate the on-premises IP requirement without VPN/ExpressRoute. NSGs cannot be applied to Key Vault as a PaaS service — they apply to VM NICs and subnets. select 'Allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass this firewall', add the specific subnets (via Service Endpoints) and the on-premises IP range, and set the default action to 'Deny'

questions.question: An organization running workloads on Azure has enabled Microsoft Defender for Cloud. The security team receives an alert: 'A process that is not usually observed has been executed on a VM.' This alert was generated without any signature matching. Which Defender for Cloud capability generated this alert?
options: Adaptive Application Controls (AAC) machine learning-based behavioral analysis detecting anomalous process execution
Just-in-Time VM access detecting unauthorized management port access attempts on the protected VM fleet at runtime
File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) detecting changes to critical system files on Windows and Linux servers continuously
Vulnerability Assessment scanning using the Qualys or Microsoft TVM integration for known CVE entries on the host
questions.explanation: Adaptive Application Controls in Defender for Cloud use machine learning to build a baseline of applications and processes that normally run on a VM. When a process outside this learned allowlist is executed, Defender for Cloud generates an alert. This is behavioral, not signature-based detection. Vulnerability Assessment identifies known CVEs and misconfigurations but does not detect runtime process anomalies. File Integrity Monitoring alerts on changes to specific monitored files (e.g., /etc/passwd), not arbitrary process execution. JIT VM Access manages port-level access and would not generate a 'process executed' alert.

questions.question: A security engineer is implementing Microsoft Entra Entitlement Management for a multinational organization. They want external users from partner organizations to be able to request access to specific internal applications through a self-service portal. The access should expire after 90 days unless renewed. Which Entitlement Management object should be configured?
options: An Entra ID B2B collaboration invite with time-limited guest account expiry in days — invites individual external users; does not govern entire connected partner organizations with a structured lifecycle access package
A Conditional Access policy requiring external users to re-authenticate on a 90-day cadence with multi-factor authentication
A PIM role setting with a 90-day maximum activation duration for external users from the partner organization
An Access Package with a policy for external users (connected organizations) setting the expiration to 90 days
questions.explanation: Entitlement Management Access Packages bundle resources (app roles, group memberships, SharePoint sites) with policies that control who can request access, approval requirements, and expiration. A policy targeting external users from connected organizations with a 90-day expiration enables the self-service portal experience described. The access automatically expires and can be configured to require renewal. PIM role settings control privileged role activation, not access package policies. Conditional Access policies control sign-in requirements and don't manage access package lifecycles. B2B invitations are account-level settings; they don't package and manage access to specific applications with governed policies.

questions.question: A security engineer needs to configure Microsoft Sentinel to automatically respond to phishing alerts by disabling the compromised user account in Microsoft Entra ID. The response should happen within minutes of the alert being triggered. Which Sentinel component implements this?
options: A Sentinel Workbook with a manual investigation workflow for the SOC team to follow when a Microsoft Graph phishing alert is triggered — requires human action; not automatic response
A Sentinel Fusion rule correlating phishing email alerts with subsequent suspicious Microsoft account sign-ins — Fusion detects multi-stage attacks but does not trigger playbook actions automatically

A Sentinel Analytics Rule with a built-in response action to disable user accounts matching phishing alerts — Analytics Rules trigger automation rules or playbooks; they have no built-in account-disable action
A Sentinel Automation Rule triggering a Playbook (Logic App) that calls the Microsoft Graph API to disable the targeted user account when a phishing alert fires
questions.explanation: Sentinel Automation Rules can be triggered when an incident is created or updated, and they can invoke a Playbook (Azure Logic App). The Logic App calls the Microsoft Graph API (specifically the `Update user` API setting `accountEnabled: false`) to disable the compromised account. This chain — incident creation → Automation Rule → Playbook → Graph API call — is the standard SOAR response pattern in Sentinel. Fusion rules create multi-stage attack incidents but have no automated response capability. Analytics Rules generate incidents but do not natively support direct entity actions like disabling accounts. Workbooks are dashboards and require manual analyst action.

questions.question: A company needs to ensure that all new Azure resources deployed in a subscription follow a naming convention and must have mandatory tags. Resources that do not comply should be prevented from being deployed. Which Azure governance tool enforces this at deployment time?
options: Azure Policy with 'Deny' effect policies for tag requirements and naming conventions applied at the subscription or management group scope — prevents non-compliant resources from being deployed

Azure Blueprints with an ARM template artifact that enforces naming conventions — applies rules via Blueprint deployment; it does not enforce tag and naming requirements on resources being deployed through non-Blueprint paths

Azure Cost Management budgets with alerts that flag subscription resources missing required tags — Cost Management monitors spending and tags after deployment; it cannot prevent non-compliant resource creation

Azure Resource Graph queries scheduled to run hourly and report non-compliant resources in the subscription — detects existing non-compliance after the fact; cannot prevent initial deployment of non-compliant resources
questions.explanation: Azure Policy with the 'Deny' effect prevents resources that don't meet the defined conditions from being deployed or modified. Policies can enforce tag presence and naming conventions at deployment time at any scope (subscription, resource group, or management group). Azure Blueprints package and deploy governance artifacts but rely on Azure Policy for enforcement — the enforcement mechanism is still Azure Policy. Azure Resource Graph is a query service for existing resources and cannot block new deployments. Azure Cost Management budget alerts are for financial monitoring and cannot prevent resource deployment.

questions.question: A security engineer is hardening an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) cluster that hosts a payment processing application. The cluster must meet PCI DSS requirements. One requirement is that the application pods must run as non-root users and must not be permitted to escalate privileges. Which Kubernetes/AKS mechanism enforces this at the pod level?
options: Microsoft Defender for Containers runtime protection — alerts when a container runs as root or with elevated privileges; it does not enforce a pod security admission policy that prevents such containers from being deployed
Kubernetes NetworkPolicy objects restricting inbound and outbound pod communication across the cluster namespaces and external endpoints
AKS Microsoft Entra integration with Kubernetes RBAC bindings that prevent developers from deploying privileged pods to production namespaces
Kubernetes Pod Security Admission (PSA) with the 'restricted' policy enforcing non-root and no privilege escalation via SecurityContext settings
questions.explanation: Kubernetes Pod Security Admission (PSA) enforces pod security standards at the namespace level. The 'restricted' profile requires pods to run as non-root users (runAsNonRoot: true) and blocks privilege escalation (allowPrivilegeEscalation: false) by rejecting pod specs that do not comply — pods failing the policy are denied at admission time. NetworkPolicy controls network traffic, not pod runtime security settings. AKS Azure AD RBAC controls who can deploy resources but does not inspect or reject pod security configurations. Defender for Containers detects and alerts on violations at runtime after the pod is already running, which is a detective control, not a preventive one.

questions.question: A subscription owner enables Microsoft Defender for Cloud at the Free (foundational CSPM) tier. Two specific capabilities REQUIRE upgrading to the enhanced security (paid) tier on the affected resource type. Which TWO capabilities require the paid tier?
options: Continuous secure-score computation across resources at the foundational tier — included in the free CSPM plan and does not require an upgrade
Just-in-Time (JIT) VM access — included with Defender for Servers (paid Defender plan)
Adaptive Network Hardening — included with Defender for Servers (paid plan), uses network telemetry to recommend NSG tightening
Free security recommendations against the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark — included in the foundational CSPM plan
questions.explanation: JIT VM access and adaptive application controls are part of Defender for Servers (paid). Secure score visualization and continuous export are available with the free Defender for Cloud baseline.
